headline: Agreed to present four Keefe Auditorium renovation or rebuilding options as choices, without endorsing any one plan.
summary: The group reviewed funding limits and four renovation or rebuilding options. A TIF plan could support a $10 million bond, leaving a $4 million gap for the lowest-cost option. No formal decision was made on funding, and the next step is gathering feedback before the July 14th presentation.

plain_text:
Keefe Auditorium Commission 
Thursday, July 2, 2026 
City Hall, Room 208 
4:30 PM 
 
 
The Keefe Auditorium Commission met on the above date in Room 208 of City Hall, called to 
order by Chairman Dennis Schneider at 4:30pm. In attendance were Shawn Smith, Dennis 
Schneider, Carl Dubois, Daniel O’Donnell, Alicia Gregg and Joseph Olefirowicz. Also in 
attendance was Amy DeRoche. Tim Cummings joined the meeting via remote connection. 
Approval of Prior Meeting Minutes 
Approval of Meeting Minutes of June 4, 2026.  Motion by Daniel O’Donnell, seconded by 
Joseph Olefirowicz, to accept minutes.  So Voted 5-0 with one abstaining. 
MEETING OVERVIEW 
Dennis distributed copies of ICON Architect’s Cost Estimates and a Cost Estimate Summary 
for the Keefe Auditorium study. He also provided a draft presentation for the Aldermanic 
meeting currently scheduled for Tuesday, July 14th. 
Project Financial Overview and Funding Constraints 
Dennis indicated that through discussions with Alderman Ben Clemons, the project’s financial 
feasibility hinges on a limited funding capacity primarily through a proposed TIF, with 
significant gaps remaining for higher-cost options. 
• TIF funding projected to support up to a $10 million bond with estimated annual tax 
revenue around $700,000, translating to approximately $1.2 million annual bond 
payments over 20 years at 3.75% interest. 
o This bond level covers only the lowest-cost project option, leaving a $4 million 
funding gap for initial purchase and development costs. 
o Higher-cost options, including full replacement or major renovations, lack a clear 
funding path under current TIF projections. 
o The TIF approach represents a way to finance the project without disrupting 
existing city capital investment frameworks. 
• Operating costs remain separate from TIF debt service, expected to be covered by a 
building operator, aligning with city reluctance to use asset revenue for operational 
expenses. 
• Current maintenance of the empty facility costs the city roughly $350,000 per year, 
highlighting urgency to repurpose or redevelop to reduce ongoing expenses. 
• No alternative funding sources secured yet, with casino or private sector contributions 
considered unlikely for large sums on short notice.
Project Options and Usage Viability 
The project team has developed four mutually exclusive renovation or rebuilding options, each 
with distinct cost, usage, and operational implications. 
• Option one (minimal renovation) estimated at approximately $16.8 million to provide 
basic upgrades including HVAC and bathrooms. 
o This option is deemed minimally useful but functional, supporting limited 
programming such as community and some performance events. 
o Pete Lolly from Spectacle Management confirmed this option can host hall acts 
despite limited dressing spaces. 
o It is unlikely to attract major Broadway tours or large-scale commercial events 
due to limited facilities and market factors. 
• Higher options involve more extensive redevelopment, increasing utilization potential 
but also escalating costs significantly, with no current financing plans to support them. 
• Phasing between options is not feasible; each represents a separate plan rather than 
stages of a single build, requiring full funding per choice. 
• The commission agreed to present all four options as a range of choices to the board, 
without endorsing any one plan, emphasizing realism balanced with aspirational arts 
community goals. 
Strategic Engagement and Presentation Planning 
A carefully staged communication and approval process with the board of aldermen and city 
administration is critical before advancing project plans. 
• Presentation to the Aldermen is scheduled for Tuesday, July 14th. 
• The team plans to present a concise slide deck summarizing work to date, options with 
pros and cons, and financial context, keeping detailed backup materials available but 
not front and center. 
• Coordination with the mayor’s office and administration is prioritized before the board 
presentation to clarify TIF feasibility and financial mechanisms. 
• Aldermen Clemens and Dowd are involved as key interlocutors, with Dowd hopefully 
assisting with discussion on TIF funding with the mayor (to avoid delays caused by 
Clemens’ current personal circumstances). 
• No formal decision is expected at the upcoming meeting; the goal is to gather feedback 
and gauge appetite for funding and further planning. 
Next Steps and Resource Requirements 
Advancing the project beyond the current assessment requires further detailed design, 
fundraising planning, and administrative approvals, all contingent on political and financial buy-
in.
• Next design phase estimated at approximately 10% of total project cost, reflecting a 
substantial, year-long effort including mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and architectural 
work. 
• Fundraising strategy development is critical but contingent on clear direction from the 
board and administration; engaging professional fundraisers would incur additional 
costs and require upfront funding. 
• The commission currently lacks in-house fundraising expertise and will need to identify 
external partners or consultants. 
• Efforts to clarify whether operating costs could be partially supported by TIF revenues or 
other mechanisms remain unresolved and will be addressed in future planning. 
• Visual materials differentiating options by footprint and interior features will be 
presented to aid aldermen’s understanding of the choices and their spatial impacts. 
Operational and Market Realities 
The project must balance aspirations for a vibrant performance venue with realistic market and 
operational constraints in the local context. 
• The local market is unlikely to attract large-scale Broadway tours due to geographic and 
demographic factors, limiting potential revenue from high-profile performances. 
• Smaller-scale programming and community uses remain viable across most options, 
supporting ongoing cultural activity while limiting financial risk. 
• Operating budgets will rely heavily on fundraising, ticket sales, and rentals, 
underscoring the need for a sustainable business model post-renovation. 
• Collaboration with experienced venue operators like Pete Ramsey’s team at the Palace 
Theater is considered a potential long-term model, leveraging nonprofit management 
expertise and existing regional networks. 
• Maintaining flexibility in development footprint and property use is critical to preserve 
future growth options and avoid constraining developers’ plans. 
Action Items 
Dennis 
• Follow up with Alderman Dowd to encourage discussion with the mayor regarding TIF 
and administration support for the project. 
• Finalize and consolidate presentation materials by July 12th for submission to Donna 
Graham for printing and distribution ahead of July 14th alderman meeting. 
• Solicit and incorporate comments on presentation draft from commission members by 
July 10-12. 
Tim 
• Assist in arranging meeting with mayor and administration early next week to discuss 
TIF feasibility.
Commission Members (General) 
• Review provided ICON materials and economic data spreadsheet for accuracy and 
provide feedback. 
• Attend July 14th alderman meeting if possible to support and observe presentation. 
Next Meeting: Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 4:30pm in room 208 of City Hall. 
Motion to adjourn by Carl Dubois, seconded by Shawn Smith. Meeting adjourned at 5:25 pm. 
Respectfully submitted, Shawn M. Smith, Auditorium Commission Secretary
